_comment: Military balancing. territory: radius of the land an occupied building claims, in the round hex metric of PathFinder.InCircle. Measured from the original maps' owner bytes (edge of the land around the buildings: tower 931, big tower 967, castle 1101 = radius squared), so the values reproduce the original.
_soldiersComment: Homestead's own combat values. damage per hit, one hit every attackSeconds; bowmen shoot up to range fields (also from the tower). Level 2/3 multiply health and damage by levelBonus.
_buildingSightComment: Fog of war: finished own buildings of these names reveal their surroundings up to this radius (other buildings only through land and settlers).
_combatPathRadiusComment: Near the enemy, soldiers plan their way within this radius around everyone standing (own soldiers too).
_combatStrengthComment: Combat strength (Kampfkraft) like the original: on own land a soldier always hits with 100 %. Elsewhere (neutral or enemy land) it starts at 100 % / number of players; goods lying on the player's own land raise it, at most to 100 %. goods: what a unit counts (per people in civilizations: Egyptians get half from gold and double from gems). The rise gets dearer: each stepPercent points of bonus cost unitsPerPercent[i] units per point (the first 10 points 1 unit each, the next 10 points 1.5 each, ...; the last value goes on). Two players need 115 gold bars for 100 % (Egyptians 230 bars or 57.5 gems).
